tip: 'Lampu kilat' = 'camera flash', the sign word – everyone just says 'flash'.
'Sesuai' = 'in accordance with' – form instruction; spoken: 'sama seperti di KTP'.
'Diserahkan' = formal 'be handed over' – counter language; spoken: 'kasih ke loket satu'.
'Petugas keamanan' = official 'security officer' – everyone actually says 'satpam'.
'Terjadi' = formal 'happens, occurs' – news and signs; spoken: 'kalau ada kebakaran'.
'Kembali' after a verb = 'back, again' in notices: 'tutup kembali' – spoken: 'tutup lagi'.
News style: 'kenaikan harga' = 'a price increase' – spoken: 'harganya naik'.
Headline verbs stand bare: 'naik' = 'has risen' – news often drops 'sudah'; add it when speaking.
'Meresmikan' = 'to officially open', from 'resmi' (official) – the ceremony verb of news.
'Wilayah' = the news word for 'area, region' – in conversation people say 'daerah'.
News passive 'diminta' = '(people) are asked to' – spoken: 'tolong hati-hati ya'.
'Meningkat' = news 'to increase' – spoken: 'naik'; 'meningkat tajam' = rose sharply.
'Pelaku' = 'perpetrator' (from 'laku', act) – crime-news vocabulary; spoken: 'pencurinya'.
'Diliburkan' = 'are given days off', official passive – spoken: 'sekolahnya libur'.
'Pemerintah kota' = 'city government' – headlines often shorten it to 'pemkot'.
'Akhir pekan' = news 'weekend' – in conversation people say 'weekend' or 'Sabtu-Minggu'.
'Pelabuhan' = 'harbor', from 'labuh' (anchor) – 'pe-…-an' builds place nouns.
'Atas' after 'menang' = 'over (an opponent)' – sports-news phrasing; spoken: 'lawan Malaysia'.
'Suku bunga' = 'interest rate', a finance-news term – 'bunga' alone is flower or interest.
'Kembali' before a verb = formal 'again' – news: 'kembali muncul'; speech: 'muncul lagi'.
'Bantuan' = 'aid', the noun of 'bantu' (help) – the '-an' ending turns verbs into nouns.
'Diperkirakan' = 'is expected, estimated' – the forecast verb of news; spoken: 'kayaknya naik'.
'Tuan rumah' = 'host (city, team)', literally 'master of the house' – sports-news idiom.
'Melanda' = news 'to strike, sweep' (weather, floods) – not for people hitting things.
'Jiwa' (soul) counts people in statistics: 'sebelas juta jiwa' = eleven million people.
'Lapangan kerja' = 'jobs, employment' (literally 'work field') – an economy-news phrase.
Invitation style: 'Bapak dan Ibu' = the formal 'you' – never 'kamu' on an invitation.
'Akan diadakan' = 'will be held', invitation passive – spoken: 'acaranya hari Minggu jam sepuluh'.
'Saudara' = very formal 'you' on invitations and forms – heard almost only in officialese.
'Kediaman' = formal 'residence' – invitations say 'kediaman', everyday speech says 'rumah'.
